correctness.rationale: The graph has four distinct open neighbors at each of its eighteen labelled vertices. I independently represented a valid code as a hitting set for the eighteen open neighborhoods and, for every distinct pair i,j, the clause {i,j} union (N(i) symmetric difference N(j)). The latter is vacuous if either vertex is selected and otherwise is equivalent to unequal signatures. This gives a different exact exhaustive predicate from the supplied programs. A row-major implementation filters all 262,144 subsets, then constructs every legal single-bit edge by removing one bit of the upper set, retaining it if the lower set passes and the upper size meets the budget. Sparse component and unweighted-distance calculations reproduce the entire degree-6-through-18 polynomial (total 103,056), the twelve alternating-column minima, and all component profiles for B=6 through 18. At B=8 there are two distinct components with six minima each; even smaller budgets cannot merge them. At B=9 there is a 22,415-state component with all minima and exactly sixty singleton states; at B=10 the 48,620 states form a single component. The clauses also show the predicate is upward closed; the independent census verifies that no inclusion-minimal code exceeds size nine. Thus a larger code can descend to size ten within the larger budget, in agreement with the explicit connectivity checks through B=18. At B=9 a state of size below nine can add a vertex, so isolates must have size nine. A size-nine isolate has no one-step deletion and, by upward closure, no valid proper subset. From each optimum the independent shortest paths give multiplicities 1,3,2,6 at distances 0,4,6,12. Same-parity minima differ by a transposition or three-cycle of omitted rows, so their symmetric difference has size four or six and a Hamming-length path through their union fits budget nine by upward closure. Opposite parities are disjoint and require at least twelve flips; the exhaustive distances attain that bound for every pair. I separately checked the provided thirteen masks for legality, capacity, the encoding, and opposite optimum endpoints; the witness alone would not prove the full profile.
residual_risks: This is a complete exact classification of one labelled torus and the at-most-budget add/delete rule, not an asymptotic theorem for general circumferences or a result about sliding or jumping tokens.

value.rationale: The first period-six tight torus in the known scalar family is a natural benchmark for incremental detector placement, not an arbitrary small graph chosen only to compute a count. The gap between universal mobility of minimum placements and full feasible-state connectivity answers two practically and mathematically different reconfiguration questions. The sixty inclusion-minimal traps witness the distinction, and the shortest-path census sharpens what is achievable at the smaller threshold. It is a useful exact finite benchmark even without an extension to larger tori.
residual_risks: No asymptotic or operational guarantee for other detector graphs or different update rules.
